pins.title: Visiting your parents this Thanksgiving? How to tell if they need more help
pins.description: Home for the Holidays: Is It Time? is an 8-page printable kit: 36 signs across six areas, the kitchen walk, three conversations that don’t start a fight, a family debrief for siblings, and a green / yellow / red guide for what to do next. $8, instant download.
pins.alt_text: Driving home for Thanksgiving with a feeling something’s changed?

pins.title: Free printable: 13 questions to ask your aging parent’s doctor
pins.description: A free one-page worksheet from The First 30 Days caregiver kit. What is the diagnosis in plain words? What should we watch for? Who do we call after hours? Check the ones that apply, add your own, write the answers during the visit. Download free, no account needed.
pins.alt_text: Free: 13 questions to ask your parent’s doctor

pins.title: Care team & contacts sheet for family caregivers (printable)
pins.description: Primary doctor, specialists, pharmacy, home health, insurance, attorney, the neighbor with a key, and every family member, with notes on best time to call. Part of The First 30 Days, a 14-page printable kit for new family caregivers. $12, instant download.
pins.alt_text: Every doctor, pharmacy and sibling on one page

pins.title: The kitchen walk: what your parent’s fridge and counters tell you
pins.description: From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time? Dates on the milk, duplicates in the pantry, scorched pans, pill bottles, the mail pile, the trash. What to look at and what it means. Printable 8-page kit, $8.
pins.alt_text: The kitchen tells you more than an hour of asking

pins.title: How to talk to aging parents about needing help: three scripts that work
pins.description: The “I noticed” opener, the future framing, and the ask for help, word for word, plus what not to say and what to do if they get angry. From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time?, an 8-page printable kit. $8.
pins.alt_text: Three ways to start the conversation without a fight

pins.title: The First 30 Days: the caregiver binder your family can share
pins.description: Roadmap, fridge sheet, contacts, medication list and log, appointments, doctor questions, documents, daily log, home safety, caregiver check-in, call log. Print it once, hand it over when someone else takes a shift. $12, instant PDF.
pins.alt_text: The binder you hand your sibling when it’s their turn

pins.title: 36 signs an aging parent may need more help (holiday visit checklist)
pins.description: The house, the kitchen, their body, mind and mood, money and mail, driving. Six signs in each area, marked privately after the visit. From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time?, an 8-page printable kit for adult children. $8.
pins.alt_text: Mom seems fine on the phone. Is she?

pins.title: Appointment tracker for caregivers: what they said, what happens next
pins.description: Date, provider, reason, what they said, next steps and follow-up date. Plus three questions to ask before you leave the office. Part of The First 30 Days caregiver kit, 14 printable pages, $12.
pins.alt_text: Write down what the doctor said before you forget it

pins.title: The family debrief: how siblings agree on what to do about Mom or Dad
pins.description: What each of you noticed (facts, not worry), where you agree, where you don’t, and three next steps with a name and a date on each. From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time?, 8 printable pages, $8.
pins.alt_text: Siblings saw different things. Compare notes within the week.

pins.title: Free one-page worksheet for your parent’s doctor visit
pins.description: Thirteen questions caregivers wish they’d asked, with room to write the answers. Free download from The First 30 Days caregiver kit.
pins.alt_text: Print this the night before Mom’s appointment

pins.title: Caregiver call log: every insurance and pharmacy call in one place
pins.description: Date, who you spoke with, about what, what was said or decided, follow-up and reference number. Because you will be asked “who told you that?” Part of The First 30 Days caregiver kit, $12.

pins.title: After the holiday visit: a green / yellow / red guide for adult children
pins.description: Count what you noticed. Green: enjoy the visit, start a baseline. Yellow: one conversation, a doctor visit within 60 days, light help first. Red: this week, not after New Year’s. From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time?, $8 printable kit.
pins.alt_text: Green, yellow or red: how fast to move after the visit

pins.title: Daily care & symptom log for caregivers (printable)
pins.description: Mood, meals, bathroom, mobility, sleep, vitals, pain scale, medications given, what to report. One page per day when something feels off. Part of The First 30 Days caregiver kit, 14 pages, $12.
pins.alt_text: Patterns show up on paper before they show up in memory

pins.title: How to check on aging parents at the holidays without an intervention
pins.description: One thing at a time. Curious, not corrective. Their life, their say. Plus what can’t wait. From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time?, an 8-page printable kit for adult children, $8.
pins.alt_text: You’re not there to inspect. You’re there for the holiday.

pins.title: How to set up a caregiver binder in one evening
pins.description: Which pages to print once (fridge sheet, contacts, medication list, documents, home safety) and which to print weekly (medication log, check-in, daily log). Three habits that make the rest easier. The First 30 Days, $12 printable kit.
pins.alt_text: Print once. Print weekly. Hand it over.

pins.title: The next steps tracker: turning a holiday worry into a January plan
pins.description: Visit date, overall color, three steps with owners and outcomes, questions for the doctor, when to look again. From Home for the Holidays: Is It Time?, $8. Pairs with The First 30 Days for the paperwork month.
pins.alt_text: New Year, same worry about Dad? Start with the paperwork.
